chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Faddal, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who visited the House (Kaaba) and did not shave his head, he said: 'He should shave it in Mecca and carry his hair to Mina, and there is nothing upon him (penalty-wise).'

And if a man shaved his head outside of Mina and did not return his hair to Mina, nothing is obligatory upon him, except that he has left the more preferable and the primary (practice). That was narrated.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets to shave his head in Mecca during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *halq* (shaving) during Hajj, distinguishing between the obligatory act and the recommended (*mustahabb*) practice of carrying the hair to Mina. It establishes that while shaving in Mecca and transporting the hair to Mina is the superior method, failing to do so does not invalidate the Hajj or incur a penalty, reflecting the Shia emphasis on distinguishing between core obligations and virtuous customs.
